explain.say: Think of a hot day in Cairo. The temperature climbs all morning, peaks in the afternoon, then falls through the night. This curve shows two days of it. Look at the yellow mark: the hottest moment, around 3 pm.

explain.say: What is special about the top? Just before it, the temperature rises. Just after, it falls. Right at the top it is flat: the slope, the derivative, is zero. A point like this is called a stationary point. Can you see the flat top?

faq.q: How do you find a maximum?
faq.a: Differentiate the function, set the derivative equal to zero and solve. Then check the slope goes from positive to negative around that point.
asks: How do I find the highest point of a curve?
How do you find maximum and minimum points?

faq.q: How can you tell a maximum from a minimum?
faq.a: Look at the slope either side. Up then down is a maximum; down then up is a minimum. Or use the second derivative: negative means maximum, positive means minimum.
asks: Is it a maximum or a minimum?

faq.a: A point where the derivative is zero, so the curve is flat for a moment. It can be a maximum, a minimum, or a point of inflection.

faq.q: Why is the derivative zero at a maximum?
faq.a: Before the top the curve rises and after it falls. In between, at the very top, the slope passes through zero.
asks: Why is the slope zero at the top?

faq.q: Can a curve have more than one maximum?
faq.a: Yes. A wavy curve like daily temperature has a high point every day. Each one is a local maximum; the highest of all is the global maximum.

facts: At a stationary point of a smooth function, the first derivative is zero.
If f′(a) = 0 and f″(a) < 0, the function has a local maximum at a.
